facts.rationale: Preserves the demonstrated constant types and values without treating source declaration order as proof of a consecutive 24-byte compiled block.
facts.value: The source defines two const Vec3 objects: it_803B8680 = { 0 } and it_803B868C = { 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.1f }. Their compiled section size, adjacency, and exact placement are not established by these declarations alone.

evidence.why: Allocation guard and ignored constructor result.

facts.rationale: Adds the exceptional construction path omitted by the previous two-outcome description.
facts.value: If article allocation returns NULL, the routine skips Chain-specific initialization and returns NULL. Otherwise it records parent_gobj, clears x10 and x14 and fifteen history vectors, processes the article model, calls it_802BAF2C with FtPart_L3rdNa, and registers attachment through Item_8026AB54 before returning the article. It discards it_802BAF2C's result: a segment-GObj construction failure does not cause this routine to return NULL or explicitly remove the allocated article.

evidence.why: Wall, ceiling, and floor mask definitions.

facts.rationale: Corrects the reversed surface classes while retaining contact, audio, neighbor guards, and exact mask behavior.
facts.value: Each call refreshes the link's map-contact state. A collision sets x2C_b1; a newly begun contact plays sound 0x41F45 only when the caller's audio gate is enabled and x2C_b2 is clear. The assignment x2C_b2 = 0xF is annotated in source as truncating to one bit, not a fifteen-frame timer. A non-colliding call clears x2C_b1 and decrements x2C_b2 if set. Floor flags (0x18000) preserve the proposed X coordinate. Otherwise wall flags (0xFFF) add the supplied Y offset only when next exists and is active and prev exists. The corrected position is written back and env_flags & 0x18FFF is returned.

facts.rationale: Replaces the incorrect ceiling-like interpretation with the canonical floor mask.
facts.value: Forwards the ItemLink, collision-audio gate, and vertical correction distance unchanged to it_802BB938 and returns its masked environment result. The delegated call mutates collision positions, contact/suppression state, and link position. The Chain physics caller masks the result with 0x18000, the floor mask, then either reverses/scales sufficiently fast vertical velocity or damps horizontal velocity and sets vertical velocity to zero.

evidence.why: Complete traversal, modes, retained values, and response.

facts.rationale: Corrects inactive-link traversal and floor classification, and preserves the last-result and zero-iteration distinctions.
facts.value: Initially advances through prev while a successor exists and the current link is inactive, selecting the first active boundary or the terminal candidate. It updates that boundary from current input history and constrains it to the anchor, then processes the remaining prev chain. Current stick axes select mode 3 when both magnitudes are below x48, otherwise mode 1 when Y < -0.5, otherwise mode 2. Collision runs only after counter > mode; counter multiples of five may use the audio gate derived from the prior x18 value, while other links disable audio. Floor flags (0x18000) cause vertical restitution above x60, otherwise x14 horizontal damping and zero vertical velocity. Each link is distance-constrained. x10 receives the final iteration's masked floor flags, not an accumulated mask; env_flags has no assignment on a path with no remaining-link iteration.

facts.rationale: Corrects the endpoint interpretation and makes the cross-file publication boundary explicit.
facts.value: Publishes the simulated Chain to its models and fighter-side hitbox updater. Starting from the first active link found from x4, it traverses prev toward the terminal free tip, writes translations and neighbor-derived orientations, scales each model's matrix basis by x4 of the article attributes, and submits sampled positions for hitbox slots 0–2 plus terminal slot 3. It does not advance link physics. Fighter-side storage and collision updates remain subject to ftSk_SpecialS_UpdateHitboxes's own guards.

evidence.why: Neighbor selection, sampling loop, and missing guards.

facts.rationale: Corrects inward/outward reversal and preserves exact sampling and precondition behavior.
facts.value: Begins at constructor head x4 and follows prev past inactive links, then traverses prev toward constructor tail x0/free tip. The attachment-side orientation sample is next->pos when next is active, otherwise the caller's anchor; the tip-side sample is prev->pos when prev exists, otherwise the current position. Direction is tip-side minus attachment-side. With stride = configured_link_count / 3, each count divisible by stride submits the current position to slots 2 down through count/stride; later boundaries overwrite progressively farther samples. The link with prev == NULL submits slot 3. There is no null guard in the initial active search and no zero-stride guard.

facts.rationale: Replaces the incorrect tail-end-driven characterization with the demonstrated state-3 role.
facts.value: Enters the deployed, input-controlled phase of Sheik's Chain after either extension phase reports list-exhaustion outcome 2. The installed callback derives its anchor from x4, the constructor head on the attachment side, and runs linked physics followed by model/hitbox publication.

facts.rationale: Corrects both tail-link terminology and unconditional restarted-animation claims.
facts.value: Enters Chain item state 3 after extension outcome 2: calls ftColl_8007AFF8 on parent_gobj, requests state 3 with ITEM_ANIM_UPDATE, then installs fn_802BB694 for attachment-side-boundary physics and transform publication. The flag does not restart an article animation here: state 3's animation ID is -1, so the common state changer removes model animations and clears the script pointer before installing callbacks.

facts.rationale: Preserves numeric-state routing while correcting reversed endpoint descriptions.
facts.value: State-1 and state-2 accessory callbacks invoke this transition when their extension helpers return 2 after exhausting the next-link list. The transition unconditionally selects item state 3 and installs fn_802BB694. The preceding callbacks start at x0, the terminal free endpoint; the destination starts from x4, the attachment-side constructor head, and its physics helper skips inactive links before propagating through prev toward the tip. The transition contains no local completion or parent-null guard.

evidence.why: State recording, conditional animation handling, and callback reset.

facts.rationale: Describes the actual Chain-specific -1 branch rather than the generic changer's untaken animation-initialization path.
facts.value: Resolves the supplied article's Item, reads seakchain.parent_gobj, and passes that fighter to ftColl_8007AFF8. It then calls Item_80268E5C with state 2 and ITEM_ANIM_UPDATE. The common changer records state 2, resets the current animation-frame field, and reads its table row. Because that row has anim_id -1, it removes model animations and clears the command-script pointer rather than initializing an animation/script. It installs the shared animation callback and null physics/collision callbacks and clears transient callbacks. This helper then assigns fn_802BB574 to on_accessory.

facts.rationale: Preserves the nested timing guard and independent removal lifetime without assuming attribute ordering.
facts.value: Unconditionally selects Chain state 4 and installs fn_802BB784. The grounded and aerial fighter ending callbacks call it only when the incremented ending counter equals x24 while also remaining strictly below x28. Equality with x28 instead calls article removal; thus coincident or reversed milestones do not imply a retraction request. State 4 repeatedly retracts and may return to state 0 when the retraction helper reports no further link, but the separately timed article-removal path does not wait for that completion.

facts.rationale: Corrects constructor endpoint terminology and keeps model-position and collision-origin initialization distinct.
facts.value: Reads seakchain.x0, the constructor tail and terminal free-end link. It transforms local (0,0,0.1) through that link's retained attachment JObj matrix and writes the resulting world position to link->pos. Separately it passes parent_gobj and coll_data.cur_pos to it_8026BB68, copies cur_pos to last_pos, marks the link active, and copies the complete supplied Vec3 into link->vel. It requests item state 1 and installs fn_802BB44C. The fighter startup caller supplies X from article attribute x50 multiplied by item facing direction, with Y and Z zero.

facts.rationale: Retains the demonstrated signature while correcting the argument-role description from constructor head to terminal endpoint.
facts.value: Chain state-entry helper with signature void(Item_GObj* gobj, Vec3* velocity). The initialized article must provide seakchain.x0, the constructor tail/terminal free-end ItemLink, its attachment JObj, and parent_gobj. The supplied Vec3 is copied into that link's initial deployment velocity; the routine returns no value.

evidence.why: Creation and launch use adjacent counter milestones.

facts.rationale: Corrects both the head-link characterization and omission of the launch offset, while distinguishing creation from launch timing.
facts.value: Begins Chain deployment by initializing the terminal free-end link x0 at a world point derived from the fighter attachment joint plus local +0.1 Z, resetting its collision history through the stored parent, activating it with caller-supplied velocity, and entering item state 1 with the extension accessory callback. Fighter startup invokes this one startup count after article creation.

facts.rationale: Corrects endpoint terminology and separates finite-list exhaustion from collision-driven routing.
facts.value: Contains no local guard: initializes and activates terminal link x0, copies the supplied velocity, and enters state 1. The fighter startup controller calls it when its counter equals the creation milestone plus one. Current and previous collision positions are made equal before deployment. Subsequent fn_802BB44C updates interpret extension outcome 1 as horizontal restitution plus entry to state 2, outcome 2 as completed next-link traversal plus entry to state 3, and outcome 0 as continuation; outcome 2 is not itself a collision classification.
